Let f(t) = −1 for t < 0 and f(t) = 1 for t ≥ 0, and set A(x) = f(t) dt. Which statement
0
about A at zero holds?
′
(A) A (0) = 1
′
(B) A (0) = −1
′
(C) A (0) = 0
(D) A is continuous but not differentiable at zero.
(E) A is discontinuous at zero.

solution.text:
For positive x, A(x) = x. For negative x, reversing the limits gives A(x) = −x. Thus
A(x) = |x|, continuous with unequal one-sided derivatives. The pointwise derivative conclu-
sion of the fundamental theorem needs continuity of the integrand at the point.
